summary: VDP-16 is a VitaDAO funding proposal (passed) for Prof. Korolchuk's lab at Newcastle University to initiate a drug discovery programme identifying novel autophagy-activating small molecules. The project uses an innovative cell-survival-based HTS assay leveraging Npc1 KO and Atg5 KO cell lines to screen a unique library of 1000+ natural compounds from northern Russia. The proposal requests £80,000–$250,000 (including TTO overhead) for a 12-month programme covering primary screening, hit verification, derivative synthesis, SAR, and target identification.

content_blocks.title: Summary & Problem Statement
content_blocks.content: Ageing is associated with decline in autophagy capacity to degrade dysfunctional cellular components (protein aggregates, mitochondria). Dysfunctional autophagy undermines DNA repair, metabolism, and survival. Lysosomal dysfunction is a key contributor to reduced autophagy during aging; when lysosomes are dysfunctional, autophagy is blocked at the terminal stage, making stimulation of autophagy initiation ineffective. Current autophagy measurement methods are unreliable, slow, and have complicated readouts, limiting screening efficiency. The proposal aims to identify novel bioactive autophagy inducers via a drug discovery programme.

content_blocks.title: Opportunity & Assay Design
content_blocks.content: Prof. Korolchuk lab uses Npc1 KO cells (mutation in lysosomal protein Npc1, associated with Niemann-Pick type C1 Disease and Parkinson's Disease) as a lysosomal dysfunction model. Under metabolic stress (galactose medium replacing glucose), these cells undergo cell death due to dysfunctional autophagy, providing a simple binary readout (cells dead/alive). Parallel use of autophagy-initiation-deficient cells (Atg5 KO) serves as a negative control to confirm true autophagy activation. If funded, the lab will screen a unique library of natural compounds, synthesize derivatives from hits, and identify biological targets.

content_blocks.title: Highlights (Proposal Strengths)
content_blocks.content: Key highlights: (1) Assay with easy readout, decent throughput, good controls targeting autophagy in cellular aging; (2) Solid evidence supporting the approach; (3) Small ticket size ($150,000–$250,000); (4) Platform enables collaboration with other autophagy/mitophagy projects; (5) Potential for IP/NFT generation from screening hits; (6) Strong scientific team interested in IP/NFT model and company formation.

content_blocks.title: Risks
content_blocks.content: Risk 1: Application relies on the natural compound library producing hits; contingency plan needed. Risk 2: Screening model relies on rescuing autophagy in a single KO model (Npc1); risk that identified compounds solve a problem specific to this KO rather than general aging. However, the team is working on addressing this risk and there are promising data suggesting it may not be a problem.

content_blocks.title: Peer Evaluation Scores
content_blocks.content: 4 independent evaluators scored the proposal: Novelty and Impact: Strong (4/4); Feasibility and Data: Outstanding (3/4), Satisfactory (1/4); Relevance to longevity: Outstanding (1/4), Strong (2/4), Satisfactory (1/4); Science Team: Strong (3/4), Satisfactory (1/4); Market Advantage: Strong (1/4), Satisfactory (2/4), Weak (1/4); IP-NFT Potential: Strong (1/4), Satisfactory (2/4), N/A (1/4). All 4 evaluators considered the project worth funding.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism of Funding
content_blocks.content: VitaDAO commits funding via an IP-NFT structure.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Background & Mechanistic Evidence
content_blocks.content: Lysosomal dysfunction (modeled by Npc1 mutation) blocks autophagy at the terminal stage. In normal glucose medium, autophagy KO cells upregulate glycolysis at the expense of mitochondrial respiration. When glucose is replaced with galactose (forcing respiration, zero net ATP from glycolysis), autophagy-deficient cells become apoptotic. This phenotype is shared by Npc1 KO MEFs (impaired autophagosome maturation) and cells lacking core autophagy genes (Atg5, Atg7, FIP200/Rb1cc1). Supporting publications: ResearchSquare rs-659023/v1; bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.01.31.928424v1 (under revision for Nature Cell Biology).

content_blocks.title: Cell Death Mechanism & Cross-Species Conservation
content_blocks.content: Established sequence of events in autophagy-deficient cell death: (1) accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria; (2) increased ROS and DNA damage; (3) activation of NADases (Sirtuin and PARP family); (4) depletion of NAD+/NADH pools; (5) mitochondrial depolarisation; (6) apoptotic cascade. This mechanism is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to humans, validated in yeast, fly, and human stem cell-derived neuronal models. Targeting downstream processes (mitochondrial dysfunction, NADase hyperactivity, NAD boosting, mitochondrial re-polarisation) rescues cell death in both Atg gene KO and Npc1 KO cells/organisms.

content_blocks.title: Proof-of-Concept Screening Data
content_blocks.content: Key experimental achievements: (1) Generated and optimized HTS-ready WT and Npc1 KO MEFs with inducible tet-on-tet-off luciferase-tagged autophagy flux reporter p62. (2) Performed proof-of-principle screen using FDA-approved drug library (Newcastle High Throughput Facility) — identified 12 small molecules previously unknown as autophagy inducers that effectively activated autophagy flux. (3) Generated and optimized WT and Npc1 KO cells stably expressing 'traffic-light' EGFP-RFP-LC3 for high-throughput high-content screening (secondary/tertiary screening platform). These results demonstrate the assay is functional and capable of identifying novel autophagy inducers.

content_blocks.title: Team
content_blocks.content: Viktor Korolchuk (VK) — cell biology, Newcastle University, UK. Jóhannes Reynisson (JR) — drug discovery, Keele University, UK. Konstantin Volcho (KPV) — organic and medicinal chemistry, Novosibirsk Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences.

content_blocks.title: Next Steps & Compound Library
content_blocks.content: KVP lab has collected 1000+ compounds isolated from rare plant and animal species from northern Russia — a virgin collection never tested for autophagy effects. Natural occurrence implies bioavailability advantage. KVP also brings in vivo testing capacity. Plan: (1) Screen ~200 diverse, readily available compounds in cell survival assays; (2) Process hits through secondary/tertiary readouts; (3) Synthesize structurally similar derivatives of hits; (4) Validate effect on autophagy in standard assays and build preliminary SAR; (5) Identify cellular targets via Samsara platform; (6) Test lead compounds in human fibroblasts and neurons for alleviation of lysosomal dysfunction-related cellular defects; (7) Test focused small molecule collections to establish robust SAR for preclinical translation.

content_blocks.title: Budget Breakdown — Lead Compound Identification (12-month programme)
content_blocks.content: Step 1: Screen ~200 natural compounds in cell survival assays (Atg5 vs Npc1 KO), dose-response (VK) — £5,000, 2 months. Step 2: Hits selection by chemical diversity, tractability, physicochemical parameters (JR) — £2,000, 1 month. Step 3: Hit verification via orthogonal assays (Luc-p62 clearance, traffic light LC3) (VK) — £3,000, 2 months. Step 4 (parallel, 2 months): Synthesis of derivatives for 3–5 hit series (~12 each) (JR, KPV) — £10,000; Additional autophagy assays (cargo degradation, flux, imaging, signalling pathways) (VK) — £5,000. Step 5: Lead series determination (VK) — £2,000, 2 months. Step 6 (parallel, 2 months): Second round synthesis ~12 derivatives (KPV, JR) — £3,000; Testing lead compounds for alleviation of lysosomal dysfunction defects (VK) — £5,000; Biological target determination (Samsara). Step 7: Screening of derivatives, SAR determination, drug lead identification (KPV, JR, VK) — £3,000, 1 month. TOTAL: 12-month postdoc + running costs = £80,000.

content_blocks.title: Future Work (Subject to Successful Screening) & IP
content_blocks.content: Step 8: ADMET/DMPK profiling in mouse models (KPV) — £16,600, 4 months: Pharmacokinetics, tissue distribution, excretion (£3,300); Routes of administration PO/IV (£3,300); Preliminary tox studies — dose-range finding, MTD (£10,000). Step 9: IP filing (patent) for drug candidate(s). TTO overhead (20–60%) not included in current budget; may increase total ticket size to $250,000. Contingency: Back-up screen of 1000+ natural bioactive compounds (KPV and VK).

key_findings: Proof-of-concept FDA-approved drug screen identified 12 novel small molecules that effectively activated autophagy flux using the Npc1 KO / Atg5 KO dual-cell-line HTS platform.
Innovative binary cell-survival assay (cells dead/alive in galactose medium) provides easy, high-throughput readout for autophagy activation, with built-in specificity control via Atg5 KO cells.
Cell death mechanism in autophagy-deficient cells is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to humans, validated in yeast, fly, and human stem cell-derived neuronal models.
KVP lab holds a unique, untested library of 1000+ natural compounds from rare northern Russian plant/animal species with inherent bioavailability advantages.
Three complementary HTS platforms established: (1) cell survival assay, (2) luciferase-tagged p62 flux reporter, (3) EGFP-RFP-LC3 'traffic-light' high-content imaging.
All 4 independent evaluators rated the project worth funding; Novelty/Impact rated Strong by all 4; Feasibility/Data rated Outstanding by 3/4.
Funding mechanism: IP-NFT via VitaDAO; total budget £80,000 (core) up to $250,000 with TTO overhead.
Future work includes ADMET/DMPK mouse model profiling and IP filing for drug candidates, contingent on successful screening.
Current TRL is approximately TRL 2–3: assay validated with proof-of-concept screen; no lead compounds yet identified from the natural compound library.
